nodes.description: SEMA6B is expressed broadly in the developing and mature brain, most strongly in cortical excitatory neurons and cerebellar Purkinje cells. In zebrafish, mosaic truncation of the last coding exon of both sema6b orthologs caused small heads, a smaller optic tectum and defective neuronal development, whereas truncation near the start codon caused only a mild phenotype. The developmental timing of the human disease, with delay before seizure onset, fits a disorder of circuit formation, but which circuits are miswired in patients has not been shown.

nodes.description: Patients show the neurophysiological signs of a hyperexcitable sensorimotor cortex typical of the progressive myoclonus epilepsies: giant or enlarged somatosensory evoked potentials, an enhanced long-latency C reflex, and myoclonic jerks preceded by a cortical potential on jerk-locked back averaging. Zebrafish carrying last-exon truncations of the sema6b orthologs were more sensitive to the convulsant pentylenetetrazole. How altered SEMA6B signalling produces this hyperexcitability, for example whether inhibitory interneurons are involved, is unknown.

nodes.description: SEMA6B binds plexin-A2 and acts as a receptor whose intracellular domain carries reverse signalling into the cell; in chick commissural neurons a SEMA6B lacking that domain cannot substitute for the full-length protein. Whether the truncated protein blocks signalling by the wild-type protein, signals aberrantly, or simply fails to signal is not established, so the node records altered signalling without a direction.

nodes.description: Disease-causing variants are heterozygous nonsense and frameshift variants clustered in exon 17, the last exon of SEMA6B, where a premature stop codon does not trigger nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. In lymphoblastoid cells from an affected individual the mutant transcript was present at a level comparable to the wild-type transcript. Truncating variants upstream of this region, which would be degraded, are seen in the general population, and SEMA6B is tolerant of loss-of-function variation; the pathogenic variant class is therefore defined by its position, not by truncation as such.

nodes.description: The only in vivo model of the disease variant class. Embryos with last-exon truncations of the sema6b orthologs had small heads, short bodies and a smaller optic tectum, and larvae showed exaggerated responses to the convulsant pentylenetetrazole; crispants targeting the start codon had a much milder phenotype. No spontaneous seizures were reported, and the animals were mosaic first-generation crispants rather than stable heterozygous lines.
